findings.description: The grader-version sort compares lists containing incompatible int and str elements. Versions such as "1.2.11" and "1.2.11-rc1" produce keys ending in 11 and "11-rc1".
findings.failure_mode: Python raises TypeError while building the batch record. Because this runs unconditionally, otherwise valid report generation aborts before either output is written.
findings.suggested_fix: Use consistently typed sort components, such as tagged tuples for numeric and textual segments, or sort version strings lexically.

findings.description: Each row matches every original and rerun directory for its task/trial, without identifying which run the row represents. A row for task-t1-r1 also counts task-t1's grade; if both runs have rows, both directories are counted twice.
findings.failure_mode: The batch's grader_versions tally includes unrepresented runs and multiplies counts when reruns are present, misreporting the grader provenance of the input rows.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve each row to its exact run directory using its run identity or rerun metadata, and count each represented run once.

findings.description: The grader_versions sort key builds a list per version by splitting on '.' and converting digit-only parts to int, leaving other parts as str. Python cannot order a list whose element at some position is int against one whose element at that position is str. Any two grade.json files whose grader_version strings differ in kind at the same position (e.g. "1.2.11" and "1.2.11-rc1", or "1.3" and "dev", or "2" and "v2") within one batch raise TypeError inside sorted(). grader_version is a free-form string read from disk, not validated anywhere in this script. The exception is not a Fail, so main() does not map it to exit 2; the report run dies with a traceback and neither report.md nor the --json twin is written, even though the batch record is documented as 'never fatal'.
findings.failure_mode: TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and 'int' raised from batch_record(); whole report aborts with an uncaught traceback instead of a written report.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a type-safe key, e.g. key=lambda kv: (kv[0] == "n/a", [(0, int(p)) if p.isdigit() else (1, p) for p in kv[0].split(".")]), so every element is a comparable (int, value) tuple. Alternatively wrap the sort in try/except TypeError and fall back to plain string ordering.

findings.description: r["arm"] from a runs.jsonl row is joined directly onto the batch directory and passed to os.listdir / isdir with no grammar check. ablation-row.sh only enforces the arm grammar under --validate; the report does not re-check it (Analysis keys cells by arm but does not reject unknown arms before batch_record runs). A row with arm "../../.." or an absolute path makes the report enumerate directories outside the batch tree and open any <name>-t<n>/grade.json it finds there. Exposure is limited to the grader_version string, but the read is outside the documented 'batch record' scope.
findings.failure_mode: Directory listing and file reads outside <batch dir> driven by row content; grader_versions tally attributed to the wrong location.
findings.suggested_fix: Only look up arms that exist in the suite (an.arms / suite arm ids), or validate r["arm"] against ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,63}$ before joining; skip and count as run_dirs_missing otherwise.

findings.description: The docstring says 1, 1.0 and "1" are one version, but only the float 1.0 is normalised; the string "1.0" (from a YAML/JSON row or from --suite-version) stays "1.0" and is a different partition key from "1". Consequences: (a) --suite-version 1.0 against rows holding integer 1 exits 2 with 'no row has that suite_version (present: 1)'; (b) rows mixing int 2 and string "2.0" are split into two versions, with "2.0" sorting as the non-numeric, highest version and becoming primary; (c) a non-integer float such as 1.5 returns None and is treated as 'absent', so among rows of another version it triggers the exit-2 'has no suite_version' message even though the row does name one.
findings.failure_mode: Spurious exit 2 or a wrong primary version / silent split of one version into two sections.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalise numeric strings fully: try float(s) and, if is_integer(), return str(int(...)); otherwise return the canonical repr of the float. Treat non-integer floats as a real version key (str(v)) rather than None. Apply the same function to --suite-version.

findings.description: A null false_positives is counted as 0 flagged regions. For an arm whose rows never recorded false_positives (rows written before that field existed, or graders that leave it null), precision computes to exactly 1.0 and usd_per_true_defect is reported as if every flagged region were a true defect. The markdown hides the precision line when false_positives_per_task is empty, but arms_json still emits precision 1.0 and usd_per_true_defect for the arm, so the JSON and the markdown disagree and a downstream reader sees a perfect precision that was never measured.
findings.failure_mode: Misleading precision = 1.0 and cost-per-true-defect in report.json for arms with no false-positive data; JSON/markdown inconsistency.
findings.suggested_fix: Only count rows where false_positives is numeric (or require at least one numeric false_positives in the arm before computing precision); otherwise set precision and usd_per_true_defect to None and record how many rows lacked the field.

findings.description: The header and render text say 'rate fallback' applies when the rows carry no per-defect ids, but the code requires every a0_bare trial of the task to have an ids/cap vector; if a single trial lacks ids (rate), the whole task drops to max-over-trials rate and the per-defect union of the other trials is discarded. For a task with trials from row writer 1.1 and 1.2 mixed, the budget-matched a0 union is understated relative to what the documentation promises.
findings.failure_mode: a0_union reported as the best single trial's rate instead of the defect union, with method 'rate fallback' on tasks that do carry per-defect ids.
findings.suggested_fix: Union over the trials that have ids/cap vectors and only fall back to rate when none does; or document that the fallback applies when any trial lacks ids and label the method 'rate fallback (mixed)'.

findings.description: budget_matched leaves e['diff'] as None for any review-catch task that has valid trials in only one of a0_bare / a1_full (a common case when one arm's cells were excluded by degradation), and render_budget still emits the row with f3(e['diff']). Elsewhere in this file f3 is only ever called on values that are non-None (interval() returns 'no pair' before calling f3). If f3 does not handle None, the report crashes with a TypeError on the format spec. This could not be confirmed from the diff because f3 is outside it.
findings.failure_mode: Possible TypeError in render_budget when a task has valid a0 trials but no valid a1 trials (or vice versa).
findings.suggested_fix: Guard the cell: 'n/a' if e['diff'] is None else f3(e['diff']) (as done for usd()), or confirm f3 handles None and add a fixture task with only one arm valid to AR-35.
